properties.project_name: SF Railyards -- Caltrain rail yard and 4th & King Station (Prologis/Caltrain redevelopment)
properties.digitized_from: Bounded by DataSF's official street centerlines (data/raw/official_street_centerlines.geojson): Townsend St (4th-7th) on the north, 4th St (Townsend-King) on the east, 7th St (Townsend-King) on the west, and King St (4th-~6th) on the south, each buffered by the project's standard measured half-width (src/street_geometry.py, 6.8m) and inset from the outer street-to-street ring by that same half-width to approximate the curb/yard edge rather than the street centerline itself -- same method as P9 (data/manual/mission_bay_p9_open_space.geojson). 2026-09-29 audit correction: the earlier text here said King St's DataSF centerline stops short of 7th St. It does not: the file has King St segments from 6th to 7th St (06TH ST -> 07TH ST, (-122.398585, 37.77289) to (-122.400804, 37.771138), plus '06TH ST - END: WEST' and 'END: EAST - 07TH ST' pieces); only the 5th-6th St segment ends at (-122.397986, 37.773324), and the next segment begins about 70 m further on. I-280 ramp segments are in the file too. The southern closing edge was drawn as a straight line from that 5th-6th point to 7th St's King-St corner and has not been re-checked against the 6th-7th St King segments (the geometry is unchanged). The resulting inset polygon is 20.08 acres, matching the SF Planning/Caltrain FAQ's own '20-acre site' description almost exactly, and its outline was checked directly against Esri World Imagery (via contextily) overlaid in QGIS-equivalent fashion -- it tracks the real fan of tracks and the 4th & King station platform canopy tightly, confirmed by the site owner 2026-09-21 after a side-by-side review of the overlay.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- not a surveyed parcel or a GIS file from Caltrain/Prologis/SF Planning. 2026-09-29 audit correction: this polygon is not free of Assessor parcels. The repo's copy of DataSF's Parcels - Active and Retired dataset (data_as_of 2026-05-31) carries three active secured-roll parcels lying wholly inside it (8701004, 700 4th St; 8701003, 311 Townsend St; 8700001, 797 7th St; together about 82% of its area), so the earlier statement that the rail right-of-way carries no block/lot was wrong. It stays an approximate feature here; whether it should instead be a real-parcel record is left to the owner. Three of the four sides (Townsend, 4th, 7th) are real, continuous DataSF street centerlines; the fourth (King St plus a straight closing line at the I-280 interchange, drawn on the earlier belief that King's DataSF centerline ended short of 7th; see the correction in digitized_from) is the weakest edge and the one most likely to need revision if a real project boundary or EIR figure becomes available. Includes the existing Caltrain 4th & King Street Station itself, which the project's own description treats as part of the site being redeveloped, not something outside it.
properties.notes: SF Planning Case No. 2023-000384CWP, 'SF Railyards Planning Program'. The 20-acre site at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square: Caltrain's northern terminus and an active service/maintenance yard, owned by Prologis with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. A Development Agreement is the expected approval path (precedent: Pier 70, Mission Rock, Potrero Power Station, all DAs). Adjoins Mission Bay North. OCII's December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map, as seen in the map image (URL added to source_doc_urls), labels N5A, N6 and N7 in this area with no land-use color and no drawn boundary, unlike the numbered Mission Bay North blocks beside it. That does not settle whether the site lies outside Mission Bay North: in the repo's copy of DataSF's redevelopment project areas layer about 41% of this polygon lies inside 'Mission Bay - North', and parcels 8701003 and 8701004 are zoned MB-O. The owner should check the map PDF and the project-area boundary.
